AUH.name: Austria (Austria-Hungary)
AUH.note: Used for the Austrian Habsburg monarchy, including when the Habsburg ruler acted as Holy Roman Emperor.

BAD.name: Baden
BAD.note: Margraviate, then Electorate and Grand Duchy, of Baden.

BAV.name: Bavaria
BAV.note: Electorate (from 1806 Kingdom) of Bavaria, before COW's 1816 start.

DEN.name: Denmark
DEN.note: Used for the united Danish-Norwegian monarchy until 1814.

FRN.name: France
FRN.note: Used for the Kingdom, the Republic and the Empire of France.

GMY.name: Germany (Prussia)
GMY.note: Used for Brandenburg-Prussia and the Kingdom of Prussia (COW 'Germany' successor).

HAN.name: Hanover
HAN.note: Electorate of Brunswick-Luneburg (Hanover), in personal union with Britain from 1714.

IRN.name: Iran (Persia)
IRN.note: Used for Persia; Peru holds the code PER in COW.

ITA.name: Italy (Sardinia)
ITA.note: Used for the Duchy of Savoy (Piedmont) and, from 1720, the Kingdom of Sardinia (COW 'Italy' predecessor).

NTH.name: Netherlands
NTH.note: Used for the United Provinces, the Batavian Republic (1795-1806) and the United Netherlands from 1813-15.

POR.name: Portugal
POR.note: Used for the Kingdom of Portugal.

RUS.name: Russia (USSR)
RUS.note: Used for Muscovy/Tsardom of Russia and the Russian Empire.

SAX.name: Saxony
SAX.note: Electorate (from 1806 Kingdom) of Saxony; Augustus II/III were also Kings of Poland.

SIC.name: Two Sicilies (Naples)
SIC.note: Used for the Bourbon Kingdom of Naples (and Sicily).

SPN.name: Spain
SPN.note: Used for Habsburg and Bourbon Spain; in the Peninsular War it means patriot Bourbon Spain, not Joseph Bonaparte's kingdom.

SWD.name: Sweden
SWD.note: Used for the Swedish Empire and Sweden (Sweden-Norway from 1814).

UKG.name: United Kingdom
UKG.note: Used for England before 1707, Great Britain 1707-1800 and the UK from 1801; in Indian wars it also stands for the British East India Company.

WRT.name: Wuerttemburg
WRT.note: Duchy, then Electorate and Kingdom, of Wurttemberg.

VNC.name: Republic of Venice
VNC.note: VEN is taken by Venezuela in COW, so VNC is used.

MYS.name: Kingdom (Sultanate) of Mysore
MYS.note: End year marks the end of independent rule (fall of Seringapatam 1799).

MNK.name: Kingdom/Principality of Montenegro (pre-1918; not in COW state system)

PRG.name: Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam

M23.name: March 23 Movement (Congo River Alliance), Rwanda-backed rebel group

wars.name: Lopez War (War of the Triple Alliance)
Off-shore Islands War (First Taiwan Strait Crisis)
Taiwan Straits War (Second Taiwan Strait Crisis)
Eighty Years' War
wars.note: Starts before 1648; included because the Peace of Munster (Jan 1648) ended it.

wars.name: Thirty Years' War
wars.note: Deaths 4.5-8 million (Wikipedia death-toll list; low end used). Denmark fought 1625-29; Saxony allied with Sweden 1631-35, then with the Emperor 1635-45 (placed on imperial side); France openly at war from 1635.

wars.name: Franco-Spanish War
wars.note: England (Protectorate) allied with France against Spain 1657-59; see Anglo-Spanish War 1654-1660.

wars.name: Portuguese Restoration War
wars.note: Starts before 1648; ended by the Treaty of Lisbon (1668), mediated by England.

wars.name: Anglo-Spanish War (1654-1660)
wars.note: c. 7,500 killed in action per side (Wikipedia infobox). France allied with England 1657-59. Hostilities ended 1660 without a treaty; formally closed by the Treaties of Madrid 1667/1670.

wars.name: Russo-Polish War (1654-1667)
wars.note: Cossack Hetmanate fought on both sides at different times (not coded).

wars.name: Second Northern War
wars.note: Brandenburg-Prussia fought with Sweden 1656-57 but against it 1655-56 and 1657-60 (placed against). Russia's part is coded separately as the Russo-Swedish War 1656-1658. Includes the Dano-Swedish wars of 1657-58 and 1658-60.

wars.name: Russo-Swedish War (1656-1658)
wars.note: Truce of Valiesar 1658; formal peace at Cardis 1661.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1663-1664)
wars.note: France sent a 6,000-man corps and League of the Rhine contingents fought on the Habsburg side (not coded).

wars.name: Polish-Ottoman War (1672-1676)
wars.note: Peace of Buczacz (1672) ended the first phase; Poland-Lithuania resumed the war in 1673; Zurawno (1676) ended it.

wars.name: Franco-Dutch War
wars.note: England fought alongside France only 1672-74 (Third Anglo-Dutch War) and then left. Sweden's part is coded as the Scanian War. Munster and Cologne fought for France (not coded).

wars.name: Third Anglo-Dutch War
wars.note: Overlaps with the Franco-Dutch War.

wars.name: Scanian War
wars.note: Northern theatre of the Franco-Dutch War; France fought on Sweden's behalf and negotiated its peace treaties.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1676-1681)
wars.note: Some Wikipedia pages date it 1672-1681.

wars.name: Great Turkish War
wars.note: Holy League war. Russia joined in 1686; its part is coded separately as the Russo-Turkish War 1686-1700. Wikipedia's casualty figures (300,000 and 90,000 killed and wounded) are not split into deaths.

wars.name: Nine Years' War
wars.note: Savoy (ITA) left the Grand Alliance by the Treaty of Turin in 1696.

wars.name: Great Northern War
wars.note: Military deaths: Sweden's side 200,000+, coalition 400,000+ (Wikipedia). Denmark fought 1700 and 1709-20; Saxony 1700-06 and from 1709; Prussia 1715-20; Hanover 1715-19. Poland-Lithuania was split, with a pro-Swedish faction 1705-09. Britain gave only naval support.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession
wars.note: Deaths 0.4-1.25 million (low end used). Savoy and Portugal joined the Grand Alliance in 1703 (Savoy had been allied with France 1701-03). Bavaria was effectively knocked out after 1704. SPN = Bourbon Spain.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1710-1713) / Pruth campaign
wars.note: Swedish and Cossack contingents fought on the Ottoman side (not coded).

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1716-1718)
wars.note: Venice had been at war with the Ottomans since 1714 (Ottoman-Venetian War 1714-18, folded in here). Wikipedia gives c. 40,000 and 80,000 killed or wounded, not deaths.

wars.name: War of the Quadruple Alliance
wars.note: Dutch Republic joined in 1719.

wars.name: Anglo-Spanish War (1727-1729)
wars.note: c. 4,600 killed (4,118 British, 492 Spanish) per Wikipedia infobox; marked major only because both sides were great powers.

wars.name: War of the Polish Succession
wars.note: Fighting ended with the preliminaries of Oct 1735; final peace at Vienna in 1738. Parma and a Prussian imperial contingent were minor participants (not coded). The Commonwealth was split between Leszczynski and Augustus III (not coded).

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1735-1739)
wars.note: Austria entered in 1737 (Austro-Turkish War 1737-39, folded in here). Ended by the Treaties of Belgrade and Nis (1739).

wars.name: War of Jenkins' Ear
wars.note: Merged into the War of the Austrian Succession from 1740; ended by Aix-la-Chapelle 1748.

wars.name: War of the Austrian Succession
wars.note: Prussia made separate peaces in 1742 (Breslau/Berlin) and 1745 (Dresden), covering the First and Second Silesian Wars. Bavaria fought with France 1741-45. Saxony was with France 1741-42 and with Austria 1743-45 (placed with Austria). Russia and Sweden fought each other separately (Russo-Swedish War 1741-43).

wars.name: Seven Years' War
wars.note: Deaths 1-1.5 million (low end used). Russia fought against Prussia until 1762, made peace and briefly allied with it (May-July 1762). Spain entered in 1761/62, Portugal in 1762, Sweden fought 1757-62 (Pomeranian War). HRE = Reichsarmee.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774)
wars.note: Large war, but no Wikipedia death total was verified, so it is marked not major under the strict criterion. The Bar Confederation fought on the Ottoman side (not coded).

wars.name: First Anglo-Maratha War
wars.note: UKG here stands for the British East India Company.

wars.name: American Revolutionary War
wars.note: Deaths 180,000-230,000 (Wikipedia death-toll list; low end used). France entered in 1778, Spain in 1779. The Dutch part is coded separately (Fourth Anglo-Dutch War). Hired German auxiliaries (e.g. Hesse-Kassel) fought for Britain (not coded).

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Dutch War
wars.note: Linked to the American Revolutionary War. The Netherlands was no longer a great power by this date (Levy).

wars.name: Second Anglo-Mysore War
wars.note: UKG = British East India Company together with Crown forces. France took part as part of the global Anglo-French war, which is why the war is marked major.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1787-1792)
wars.note: Wikipedia infobox lists 59,000-72,000 killed for one side, so the death total exceeds 50,000; the per-side split is unclear, so no single estimate is given. Austria's part is coded separately (Austro-Turkish War 1788-1791).

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1788-1791)
wars.note: Austria declared war in Feb 1788 as Russia's ally; Wikipedia lists it as 1787-1791.

wars.name: Russo-Swedish War (1788-1790)
wars.note: Denmark-Norway briefly attacked Sweden in 1788 (Theatre War; not coded).

wars.name: Third Anglo-Mysore War
wars.note: UKG = British East India Company; Hyderabad and Travancore also fought against Mysore (not coded).

wars.name: Polish-Russian War of 1792
wars.note: The Targowica Confederation sided with Russia; the war was followed by the Second Partition (1793).

wars.name: War of the First Coalition
wars.note: Prussia and Spain left in 1795 (Basel); Spain then allied with France (1796). The Dutch Republic fought France 1793-95 and then became the Batavian Republic, a French ally (placed with the coalition). Sardinia left in 1796. Britain fought on alone after Campo Formio.

wars.name: Kosciuszko Uprising (Polish-Russian/Prussian War of 1794)
wars.note: Followed by the Third Partition (1795).

wars.name: War of the Second Coalition
wars.note: Russia withdrew in 1799; Austria and Naples made peace in 1801. Spain fought Britain and Portugal (War of the Oranges, 1801) as France's ally.

wars.name: Quasi-War
wars.note: Undeclared naval war.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
wars.note: UKG = British East India Company; Hyderabad fought with the British. Ended with Tipu Sultan's death at Seringapatam; no peace treaty.

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition
wars.note: Wikipedia gives 160,000 coalition and 62,050 French-side casualties (killed, wounded and captured), not deaths.

wars.name: War of the Fourth Coalition
wars.note: Saxony fought with Prussia until Dec 1806 and then joined France (placed with France). Confederation of the Rhine contingents fought with France (not coded).

wars.name: Peninsular War
wars.note: Deaths over 1,000,000 including civilians (Wikipedia). Some sources date the start to Oct 1807. SPN = patriot (Bourbon) Spain.

wars.name: War of the Fifth Coalition
wars.note: Britain's part was the Walcheren expedition and the Peninsula; Russia was nominally allied with France (not coded).

wars.name: French invasion of Russia
wars.note: Dead: French side 300,000-350,000, Russia 210,000 (Wikipedia infobox; low end summed). Austria and Prussia supplied auxiliary corps under the 1812 alliances with France.

wars.name: War of 1812
wars.note: Deaths from all causes: US up to 15,000, UK c. 10,000, Indigenous allies c. 10,000 (Wikipedia infobox). Formally ended with ratification in Feb 1815.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.note: Wikipedia dates it from 24 Dec 1812; Prussia declared war on 13 Mar 1813 and Austria joined in Aug 1813. Bavaria (Treaty of Ried, Oct 1813), Saxony (at Leipzig) and Wurttemberg (late 1813) switched to the coalition but fought longer with France. Denmark made peace at Kiel in Jan 1814. Combat casualties were c. 526,000 coalition and 610,000 French side (not deaths).

wars.name: War of the Seventh Coalition (Hundred Days)
wars.note: Russian armies entered France after Waterloo and saw little combat. Several smaller states joined only nominally (not coded).

wars.name: Russo-Georgian War
wars.note: 7-12 Aug 2008; South Ossetian and Abkhaz forces fought alongside Russia. EU-mediated six-point ceasefire.

wars.name: Djiboutian-Eritrean border conflict
wars.note: Clashes 10-13 Jun 2008 at Ras Doumeira; Djibouti reported 44 own dead and ~100 Eritrean dead. Qatar-mediated agreement 6 Jun 2010.

wars.name: Heglig Crisis (Sudan-South Sudan border war)
wars.note: Mar-Sep 2012; South Sudan seized Heglig oilfield, withdrew 20 Apr 2012. Death claims range from 31/256 (South Sudanese) to 1,200 (Sudanese); no reliable total.

wars.name: Russo-Ukrainian War: Crimea annexation and Donbas war
wars.note: Crimea seized Feb-Mar 2014; Donbas war fought largely via Russian-backed DPR/LPR with direct Russian army involvement (e.g., Ilovaisk 2014, Debaltseve 2015). Merged into the full-scale invasion on 24 Feb 2022. Deaths ~14,000 (UN OHCHR 2014-2021 estimate, from prior knowledge; not re-fetched).

wars.name: 2016 Nagorno-Karabakh clashes (Four-Day War)
wars.note: 1-5 Apr 2016; US State Department estimate ~350 dead on both sides. Ceasefire agreed in Moscow 5 Apr 2016.

wars.name: Operation Spring Shield (Turkey-Syria clashes in Idlib)
wars.note: 27 Feb-6 Mar 2020; ~40 Turkish soldiers (33 in the Balyun airstrike) and 197-405 Syrian government/allied fighters killed (SOHR / MEI). Ended by Turkey-Russia Moscow ceasefire 5 Mar 2020.

wars.name: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
wars.note: 27 Sep-10 Nov 2020 (44 days); official military deaths 3,825 Armenian/Artsakh and 2,906 Azerbaijani plus ~185 civilians. Turkey supported Azerbaijan; Syrian mercenaries also deployed.

wars.name: Russian invasion of Ukraine
wars.note: Full-scale war from 24 Feb 2022, ongoing as of Oct 2026 (local Oleshky ceasefire agreed 24 Oct 2026; talks planned Nov 2026). North Korean troops fought for Russia in Kursk 2024-25. CSIS (Jan 2026): up to 325,000 Russian and 140,000 Ukrainian military deaths Feb 2022-Dec 2025.

wars.name: 2022 Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan border war
wars.note: Main fighting 14-20 Sep 2022 (earlier clashes Jan-Jun 2022); 83 Tajik and 63 Kyrgyz deaths reported. Border treaty signed 13 Mar 2025.

wars.name: September 2022 Armenia-Azerbaijan clashes
wars.note: 12-14 Sep 2022, Azerbaijani strikes into Armenia proper; ~204 Armenian servicemen and 80 Azerbaijani servicemen killed, plus civilians.

wars.name: Rwanda-backed M23 offensive in eastern DR Congo
wars.note: Rwandan Defence Force units operated alongside M23 (documented by UN experts); Goma fell Jan 2025, Bukavu Feb 2025. Deaths ~7,000 since Jan 2025 per DRC government claim (prior knowledge). Washington peace agreement 27 Jun 2025 and Washington Accords 4 Dec 2025; fighting continued (M23 took Uvira Dec 2025). Interstate status is contested (Rwanda denies direct combat role).

wars.name: 2023 Azerbaijani offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh
wars.note: 19-20 Sep 2023; 192 Azerbaijani and 200+ Artsakh soldiers killed. Armenia not a belligerent; Artsakh dissolved and nearly all Armenians left. Not strictly interstate (one side non-recognised).

wars.name: Iran-Israel direct strikes of 2024
wars.note: Iranian missile/drone attacks 13-14 Apr and 1 Oct 2024; Israeli strikes 19 Apr and 26 Oct 2024. Few deaths (several Iranian soldiers killed 26 Oct). From prior knowledge; not re-fetched (search budget exhausted).

wars.name: 2025 India-Pakistan conflict (Operation Sindoor)
wars.note: 7-10 May 2025; official tolls 29 Indian (21 civilians) and 53 Pakistani (40 civilians). Ceasefire agreed via DGMO hotline 10 May 2025.

wars.name: Twelve-Day War (Israel-Iran war)
wars.note: 13-24 Jun 2025; US struck Iranian nuclear sites 22 Jun. Iran 1,060-1,190 dead, Israel ~33. US-brokered ceasefire 24 Jun 2025.

wars.name: Cambodia-Thailand border conflict (July 2025)
wars.note: 24-28 Jul 2025; early official tolls ~16 Thai soldiers, 14 Thai civilians, 5 Cambodian soldiers, 8 Cambodian civilians (OSINT suggests higher Cambodian military losses). Malaysia-brokered Putrajaya ceasefire 28 Jul 2025.

wars.name: October 2025 Afghanistan-Pakistan border clashes
wars.note: ~9-19 Oct 2025; Pakistani strikes on Kabul/Kandahar and border fighting, dozens of troops and civilians killed (e.g., 40 civilians in Spin Boldak per local officials). No reliable total. 48-hour truce 15 Oct, Doha ceasefire 19 Oct 2025 (Qatar/Turkey).

wars.name: Cambodia-Thailand border conflict (December 2025)
wars.note: 8-27 Dec 2025; Thailand: 26 soldiers + 1 civilian in combat and 44 indirect civilian deaths; Cambodia: 30 civilians and 110+ soldiers/police (Nikkei count). Ceasefire signed by defence ministers 27 Dec 2025.

wars.name: 2026 United States intervention in Venezuela
wars.note: 3 Jan 2026 strikes and raid that captured Nicolas Maduro; ~80 dead (23-47 Venezuelan military, 32 Cuban personnel, civilians), no US deaths. A brief interstate armed clash rather than a sustained war; relations restored Mar 2026.

wars.name: 2026 Afghanistan-Pakistan war
wars.note: From 21 Feb 2026 ('open war' declared 27 Feb); Pakistan claimed ~800 Afghan Taliban/TTP fighters killed by 5 Apr 2026, Taliban claimed 400+ killed in a March strike on a Kabul rehab centre; figures unverified, total highly uncertain. Eid pause in March; front reported quiet after Chinese-hosted Urumqi talks mid-Apr 2026 with no settlement. end=null because no settlement is recorded and a search hit (FDD, dated 5 Oct 2026, unfetchable) suggests renewed Pakistani strikes in autumn 2026.

wars.name: 2026 Iran war
wars.note: From 28 Feb 2026 (US-Israeli strikes; Ali Khamenei killed). Gulf states listed as belligerents after Iranian strikes on their territory. Iran deaths 3,528-3,684 (Iranian govt/HRANA) to 6,000+ military (US/Israeli claim); all fronts incl. Israel-Hezbollah in Lebanon 8,000-10,600 (deaths_est = rough midpoint, all fronts). Ceasefire 8 Apr, Islamabad MoU 17 Jun, collapse 8 Jul 2026; as of Oct 2026 strikes largely halted but no deal and a US blockade continues. major=false is borderline: all-front estimates straddle 10,000 and only one side is a great power.

treaties.name: Peace of Munster
treaties.summary: Spain recognised the independence of the Dutch Republic, ending the Eighty Years' War; signed within the Westphalian congress (date from memory, not verified in this session).

treaties.name: Peace of Westphalia (Treaties of Osnabruck and Munster)
treaties.summary: Ended the Thirty Years' War in the Empire, with territorial gains for France, Sweden, Brandenburg and Bavaria and confirmed rights for the imperial estates; the Franco-Spanish war continued. Brandenburg (GMY), Bavaria and Saxony are listed as imperial estates.

treaties.name: Treaty of Westminster (1654)
treaties.summary: Ended the First Anglo-Dutch War between the English Commonwealth and the United Provinces (5/15 April 1654).

treaties.name: Treaty of Paris (1657)
treaties.summary: Cromwell's England and Louis XIV's France allied against Spain (exact day not verified).

treaties.name: Treaty of Roskilde

violated.how: Charles X Gustav renewed the attack on Denmark-Norway in August 1658, in defiance of the treaty.

treaties.summary: Denmark-Norway ceded Scania, Halland, Blekinge, Bohuslan, Bornholm and Trondelag to Sweden, ending the Dano-Swedish War of 1657-58 (26 Feb O.S./8 Mar N.S.).

treaties.name: Treaty of the Pyrenees
treaties.summary: Ended the Franco-Spanish War begun in 1635; France gained Roussillon and Artois and Louis XIV married Maria Theresa.

treaties.name: Treaty of Copenhagen (1660)
treaties.summary: Ended the Dano-Swedish War of 1658-60; Bornholm and Trondelag returned to Denmark-Norway, while Sweden kept Scania, Halland, Blekinge and Bohuslan.

treaties.name: Treaty of Oliva
treaties.summary: Peace among Sweden, Poland-Lithuania, the Habsburgs and Brandenburg-Prussia; Poland recognised Swedish Livonia and Prussian sovereignty.

treaties.name: Treaty of Cardis
treaties.summary: Russia and Sweden restored the pre-war borders, formally ending the Russo-Swedish War of 1656-58 (exact day not verified).

treaties.name: Peace of Vasvar
treaties.summary: Twenty-year Habsburg-Ottoman peace after the Battle of Saint Gotthard, leaving the Ottomans their recent gains in Hungary (date taken as the war's end date in Wikipedia).

treaties.name: Treaty of Breda (1667)
treaties.summary: Three bilateral treaties between England and the Dutch Republic, France and Denmark-Norway ended the Second Anglo-Dutch War; England kept New Amsterdam and the Dutch kept Suriname.

treaties.name: Truce of Andrusovo
treaties.summary: A 13.5-year truce giving Russia Smolensk, Left-bank Ukraine and (temporarily) Kiev.

treaties.name: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1668)
treaties.summary: Ended the War of Devolution; France kept towns in the Spanish Netherlands but returned Franche-Comte, under Triple Alliance mediation.

treaties.name: Treaty of Lisbon (1668)
treaties.summary: Spain recognised Portugal's independence under the House of Braganza, with English mediation.

treaties.name: Triple Alliance (1668)

violated.how: England secretly undertook at Dover (1670) to abandon the alliance and in 1672 joined France in attacking the Dutch Republic.

treaties.summary: England and the Dutch Republic (Sweden joined in May 1668) combined to force France to end the War of Devolution.

treaties.name: Secret Treaty of Dover
treaties.summary: Charles II secretly agreed to join Louis XIV in attacking the Dutch Republic and to convert to Catholicism, in return for French subsidies.

treaties.name: Treaty of Madrid (1670)
treaties.summary: Anglo-Spanish peace in which Spain recognised English possession of Jamaica and the Cayman Islands, formally closing the war of 1654-60 (8 July O.S./18 July N.S.).

treaties.name: Peace of Buczacz

violated.how: The Sejm refused to ratify the treaty and Poland-Lithuania resumed the war in spring 1673.

treaties.summary: Poland-Lithuania ceded Podolia and agreed to pay tribute to the Ottomans, ending the first phase of the war.

treaties.name: Treaty of Westminster (1674)
treaties.summary: Ended the Third Anglo-Dutch War; England left the war against the Dutch Republic and New Netherland was returned to England (9 Feb O.S./19 Feb N.S.).

treaties.name: Treaty of Zurawno
treaties.summary: Revised the Buczacz terms and ended the Polish-Ottoman War; the Ottomans kept Podolia.

treaties.name: Treaties of Nijmegen
treaties.summary: Series of treaties (France-Dutch 10 Aug 1678, France-Spain 17 Sep 1678, France/Sweden-Emperor 5 Feb 1679, and others) ending the Franco-Dutch War; France gained Franche-Comte.

treaties.name: Peace of Lund
treaties.summary: Direct Dano-Swedish peace reaffirming the Fontainebleau terms and ending the Scanian War (16 Sep O.S./26 Sep N.S.).

treaties.name: Treaty of Fontainebleau (1679)
treaties.summary: France, acting for Sweden, made Denmark-Norway return its Swedish conquests (23 Aug O.S./2 Sep N.S.).

treaties.name: Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye (1679)
treaties.summary: Brandenburg returned most of its conquests in Swedish Pomerania under French pressure (19 June O.S./29 June N.S.).

treaties.name: Treaty of Bakhchisarai
treaties.summary: Twenty-year truce setting the Russo-Ottoman border on the Dnieper (3 Jan O.S./13 Jan N.S.).

treaties.name: Holy League (1684)
treaties.summary: Anti-Ottoman alliance of the Habsburgs, Poland-Lithuania and Venice under papal patronage, signed at Linz; Russia joined in 1686.

treaties.name: Truce of Ratisbon

violated.how: Louis XIV ended the twenty-year truce after four years by invading Philippsburg in September 1688, which started the Nine Years' War.

treaties.summary: Twenty-year truce leaving France in possession of Strasbourg and the Reunion gains, ending the War of the Reunions.

treaties.name: Eternal Peace of 1686 (Treaty of Grzymultowski)
treaties.summary: Confirmed Andrusovo, with Kiev going permanently to Russia, and brought Russia into the anti-Ottoman Holy League.

treaties.name: League of Augsburg
treaties.summary: Defensive league of the Emperor, imperial circles, Spain (for the Burgundian Circle), Sweden (for Swedish Pomerania) and Bavaria against French expansion (exact day not verified).

treaties.name: Grand Alliance (Treaty of Vienna, 1689)
treaties.summary: Emperor Leopold I and the Dutch Republic allied against France; England acceded in Dec 1689, Spain and Savoy in 1690.

treaties.name: Treaty of Turin (1696)
treaties.summary: Separate peace in which Savoy left the Grand Alliance and France returned Pinerolo and Savoy's occupied lands.

treaties.name: Peace of Ryswick
treaties.summary: Ended the Nine Years' War: treaties of 20-21 Sep 1697 with Spain, England and the Dutch, and of 30 Oct 1697 with the Emperor; France recognised William III.

treaties.name: Treaty of The Hague (1698), First Partition Treaty
treaties.summary: England, France and the Dutch Republic agreed in advance how to partition the Spanish monarchy on Charles II's death.

treaties.name: Treaty of Karlowitz
treaties.summary: The Ottomans ceded most of Hungary and Transylvania to the Habsburgs, Podolia to Poland and the Morea to Venice; Russia agreed only a truce.

treaties.name: Treaty of Preobrazhenskoye
treaties.summary: Secret alliance between Peter I and Augustus II (as Elector of Saxony and King of Poland) against Sweden, preparing the Great Northern War.

treaties.name: Peace of Travendal

violated.how: Denmark-Norway re-entered the war against Sweden in 1709, after Poltava.

treaties.summary: Separate peace that took Denmark-Norway out of the Great Northern War and restored Holstein-Gottorp, with the Maritime Powers among the guarantors.

treaties.name: Treaty of Constantinople (1700)
treaties.summary: Russia gained Azov and Taganrog and was freed from paying tribute to the Crimean Khan (3 July O.S./13 July N.S.).

treaties.name: Treaty of London (1700), Second Partition Treaty
treaties.summary: Revised Spanish partition plan giving Spain and the Indies to Archduke Charles and Italian lands to France.

treaties.name: Treaty of The Hague (1701), Grand Alliance
treaties.summary: England, the Emperor and the Dutch Republic renewed the Grand Alliance against a Bourbon succession in Spain.

treaties.name: Methuen Treaty (military alliance)
treaties.summary: Portugal joined the Grand Alliance in May 1703 (exact day not verified); a separate Anglo-Portuguese commercial treaty followed on 27 Dec 1703.

treaties.name: Treaty of Altranstadt (1706)

violated.how: After Poltava, Augustus II re-entered the war and renewed his Russian alliance at Thorn (1709), which Altranstadt had dissolved.

treaties.summary: Augustus II gave up the Polish crown and his Russian alliance, taking Saxony out of the war.

treaties.name: Treaty of Thorn (1709)
treaties.summary: Peter I and Augustus II revived their anti-Swedish alliance and agreed to restore Augustus to the Polish throne.

treaties.name: Treaty of the Pruth
treaties.summary: After the encircled Russian army was allowed to withdraw, Peter I agreed to return Azov; confirmed by the Treaty of Adrianople (1713). Some sources date it 21 July.

treaties.name: Peace of Utrecht
treaties.summary: Series of treaties (France with Britain, the Dutch, Prussia, Savoy and Portugal on 11 Apr 1713; Spain with Britain and Savoy on 13 Jul 1713, the Dutch in 1714 and Portugal in 1715) recognising Philip V on condition the French and Spanish crowns stayed separate.

treaties.name: Treaty of Baden (1714)
treaties.summary: Ended hostilities between France and the Holy Roman Empire as a body.

treaties.name: Treaty of Rastatt
treaties.summary: Franco-Habsburg peace giving Austria the Spanish Netherlands, Milan, Naples and Sardinia.

treaties.name: Triple Alliance (1717)
treaties.summary: Britain, France and the Dutch Republic allied to uphold the Utrecht settlement against Bourbon Spain.

treaties.name: Quadruple Alliance (1718)
treaties.summary: Britain, France and Austria (with Savoy, and the Dutch joining later) allied to reverse Spain's attacks on Sardinia and Sicily.

treaties.name: Treaty of Passarowitz
treaties.summary: Austria gained the Banat, northern Serbia including Belgrade, and Lesser Wallachia, and Venice lost the Morea; also ended the Ottoman-Venetian War of 1714-18.

treaties.name: Treaty of Stockholm (1719)
treaties.summary: Sweden ceded Bremen-Verden to Hanover.

treaties.name: Treaty of Frederiksborg
treaties.summary: Dano-Swedish peace in which Sweden gave up its exemption from the Sound Toll and its support for Holstein-Gottorp (3 July O.S./14 July N.S.).

treaties.name: Treaty of Stockholm (1720)
treaties.summary: Sweden ceded southern Swedish Pomerania, including Stettin, Usedom and Wollin, to Prussia.

treaties.name: Treaty of The Hague (1720)
treaties.summary: Spain acceded to the Quadruple Alliance; Savoy exchanged Sicily for Sardinia with Austria.

treaties.name: Treaty of Nystad
treaties.summary: Sweden ceded Livonia, Estonia, Ingria and part of Karelia to Russia, ending the Great Northern War (30 Aug O.S./10 Sep N.S.).

treaties.name: Treaty of Hanover (1725)
treaties.summary: Defensive alliance of Britain-Hanover, France and Prussia set against the Austro-Spanish Vienna alliance; the Dutch joined in 1726 and Sweden in 1727.

treaties.name: Treaty of Vienna (1725)
treaties.summary: Four treaties (30 Apr-5 Nov 1725) made peace between Charles VI and Philip V and created an Austro-Spanish alliance backing the Ostend Company and the Pragmatic Sanction; Russia joined in 1726.

treaties.name: Treaty of Seville
treaties.summary: Ended the Anglo-Spanish War of 1727-29 on a status quo basis; the Dutch acceded on 29 Nov 1729.

treaties.name: Treaty of Vienna (1731)
treaties.summary: Created the Anglo-Austrian alliance: Britain and the Dutch guaranteed the Pragmatic Sanction and Austria dissolved the Ostend Company; Spain signed on 22 July.

treaties.name: Treaty of Turin (1733)
treaties.summary: Secret Franco-Sardinian alliance to seize Milan from Austria at the start of the War of the Polish Succession.

treaties.name: Treaty of the Escorial (First Family Compact)
treaties.summary: First Bourbon Family Compact between Louis XV and Philip V.

treaties.name: Treaty of Vienna (1738)
treaties.summary: Final peace of the War of the Polish Succession: Augustus III kept Poland, Leszczynski received Lorraine (to pass to France), Francis Stephen received Tuscany and the Spanish Bourbons Naples-Sicily.

treaties.name: Treaty of Belgrade
treaties.summary: Austria returned northern Serbia, including Belgrade, and Lesser Wallachia to the Ottomans.

treaties.name: Treaty of Nis (1739)
treaties.summary: Russia kept Azov (to be demilitarised) but gave up most of its other conquests.

treaties.name: Treaty of Breslau/Berlin (1742)
treaties.summary: Separate peace ending the First Silesian War; Austria ceded most of Silesia (preliminaries at Breslau on 11 June).

treaties.name: Treaty of Abo
treaties.summary: Sweden ceded part of south-eastern Finland to Russia (7 Aug O.S./18 Aug N.S.).

treaties.name: Treaty of Fontainebleau (1743) (Second Family Compact)
treaties.summary: Second Bourbon Family Compact, signed during the War of the Austrian Succession.

treaties.name: Treaty of Worms (1743)
treaties.summary: Britain, Austria and Sardinia allied in the War of the Austrian Succession.

treaties.name: Treaty of Dresden
treaties.summary: Ended the Second Silesian War, confirming Prussian possession of Silesia.

treaties.name: Treaty of Fussen
treaties.summary: Separate peace in which Bavaria gave up its imperial claims and left the war.

treaties.name: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748)

judgment.rationale: Many historians see the treaty as an armistice rather than a settlement: it left Maria Theresa determined to recover Silesia and the colonial disputes unresolved, which led to the Diplomatic Revolution and the Seven Years' War.

treaties.summary: Ended the War of the Austrian Succession largely on a status quo basis, but left Silesia with Prussia. Signed by Britain, France and the Dutch; Austria, Spain and Sardinia acceded in Dec 1748 and Genoa and Modena in Jan 1749.

treaties.name: Convention of Westminster (1756)
treaties.summary: Britain and Prussia agreed to keep foreign troops out of Germany, protecting Hanover; this neutrality pact set off the Diplomatic Revolution.

treaties.name: First Treaty of Versailles (1756)
treaties.summary: Franco-Austrian defensive alliance and neutrality pact (24,000 troops if either was attacked), the core of the Diplomatic Revolution.

treaties.name: Second Treaty of Versailles (1757)
treaties.summary: Offensive Franco-Austrian alliance against Prussia.

treaties.name: Third Family Compact (Treaty of Paris, 1761)
treaties.summary: Bourbon alliance between Charles III and Louis XV that brought Spain into the Seven Years' War.

treaties.name: Treaty of Hamburg (1762)
treaties.summary: Ended the Pomeranian War between Sweden and Prussia on a status quo basis.

treaties.name: Treaty of Saint Petersburg (1762)
treaties.summary: Peter III made peace with Prussia and returned Russian conquests, taking Russia out of the war.

treaties.name: Treaty of Hubertusburg
treaties.summary: Ended the Third Silesian War on a status quo basis, with Prussia keeping Silesia.

treaties.name: Treaty of Paris (1763)
treaties.summary: Ended the Seven Years' War overseas: France ceded Canada and lands east of the Mississippi to Britain, and Spain ceded Florida to Britain.

treaties.name: First Partition of Poland (treaty)
treaties.summary: Russia, Prussia and Austria annexed about a third of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth's territory (ratified 22 Sep 1772).

treaties.name: Treaty of Kucuk Kaynarca
treaties.summary: Russia gained Kerch, Yenikale and part of Yedisan and access to the Black Sea, and the Crimean Khanate was declared independent of the Ottomans (10 Jul O.S./21 Jul N.S.).

treaties.name: Treaty of Alliance (1778)

violated.how: Congress unilaterally annulled the perpetual alliance on 7 July 1798 during the Quasi-War crisis; it was formally abrogated at Mortefontaine in 1800.

treaties.summary: Perpetual Franco-American military alliance against Britain, signed in Paris.

treaties.name: Treaty of Aranjuez (1779)
treaties.summary: Spain agreed to join France in the war against Britain.

treaties.name: Treaty of Teschen
treaties.summary: Austria gained only the Innviertel; France and Russia mediated and guaranteed the treaty. Saxony, Prussia's co-belligerent, is not coded as a party because its role in the treaty was not verified.

treaties.name: First League of Armed Neutrality
treaties.summary: Russia, Denmark-Norway and Sweden combined to protect neutral shipping against British searches; Prussia, Austria and Portugal joined in 1781-82 and Naples in 1783.

treaties.name: Treaty of Salbai
treaties.summary: Ended the First Anglo-Maratha War largely on a status quo basis (UKG = British East India Company).

treaties.name: Peace of Paris (1783)
treaties.summary: Britain recognised US independence (Treaty of Paris) and made peace with France and Spain at Versailles; Spain kept Minorca and the Floridas.

treaties.name: Treaty of Mangalore
treaties.summary: Tipu Sultan and the East India Company restored the status quo ante, ending the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

treaties.name: Treaty of Paris (1784)
treaties.summary: The Dutch ceded Negapatnam to Britain and granted free navigation in the Moluccas, ending the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War.

treaties.name: Triple Alliance (1788)
treaties.summary: The Anglo-Prussian alliance of 13 Aug 1788, together with both powers' 1788 agreements with the restored Orangist Dutch Republic, formed the Triple Alliance.

treaties.name: Treaty of Varala
treaties.summary: Ended the Russo-Swedish War of 1788-90 on a status quo basis (date from memory; year confirmed in Wikipedia's List of treaties).

treaties.name: Treaty of Sistova
treaties.summary: Austria returned its conquests, including Belgrade, to the Ottomans (date from memory; year confirmed in Wikipedia's List of treaties).

treaties.name: Treaty of Jassy
treaties.summary: The Ottomans recognised the Russian annexation of Crimea and ceded Yedisan up to the Dniester.

treaties.name: Treaty of Seringapatam
treaties.summary: Tipu Sultan ceded about half his territory to the East India Company, the Marathas and Hyderabad.

treaties.name: Second Partition of Poland (treaty)
treaties.summary: Russia and Prussia annexed large parts of the Commonwealth; the annexations were forced through the Grodno Sejm.

treaties.name: Jay Treaty

treaties.name: Peace of Basel (France-Prussia)
treaties.summary: Separate peace taking Prussia out of the First Coalition and leaving the French on the left bank of the Rhine.

treaties.name: Peace of Basel (France-Spain)
treaties.summary: Ended the War of the Pyrenees; Spain ceded its part of Santo Domingo to France.

treaties.name: Third Partition of Poland (treaty)

treaties.name: Second Treaty of San Ildefonso
treaties.summary: Franco-Spanish offensive and defensive alliance against Britain (date from memory; year confirmed in Wikipedia's List of treaties).

treaties.name: Treaty of Campo Formio

treaties.name: Second League of Armed Neutrality

treaties.name: Treaty of Mortefontaine (Convention of 1800)

treaties.name: Treaty of Luneville
